title: fix(meetings): keep meeting audio capture alive after the join request responds
body:
Root cause: `src/meeting-bot/realtime-browser-audio-transport.ts:127` (and its `stop` at `:75`, plus the node bridge's `invoke` at `src/meeting-bot/realtime-node-audio-transport.ts:38`) dispatches the recurring capture `pull`, the final `stop` and every chrome-node bridge command from the async context of the request that joined the meeting, so once `googlemeet.join` (or the agent tool turn) finishes, the Gateway refuses those calls and the live-voice bridge closes.

Fixes #173896
Refs #167246 (same mechanism on the Zoom tool path; see Evidence)

## What Problem This Solves

In a `bidi` meeting that uses managed browser audio capture (no `chrome.audioInputCommand`), the bot joins, says its greeting, and then goes deaf about 300 ms after the join call returns. The Gateway logs `Meeting browser audio capture failed: Gateway requester authority changed` (or `Browser requester is no longer active`), the realtime bridge closes, and participant speech never reaches the model. The chrome-node transport fails the same way with `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching node.invoke`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transports are created inside the join request, and their recurring browser and node calls inherit that request's context. In-process dispatch resolves the ambient request (and operator tool) authority, which closes when the join responds.

Work that outlives a plugin call already has an owner on `main`: the plugin instance's background context (`api.lifecycle.runInBackgroundContext`, docs: plugins/sdk-runtime "instance-bound background context"). Meeting transcript capture moved onto it for the same failure in #178415. This PR puts audio capture pulls, capture cleanup and node bridge commands on the same owner:

- `captureCurrentPluginBackgroundRunner()` (in `plugin-instance-invocation.ts`) returns the active plugin call's background runner, or runs inline outside a plugin call. The transcript bridge, browser capture and node bridge now share it instead of inlining the lookup.
- The join-time capture `start` still runs under the joining request, so authority is checked once when the session starts, as `AGENTS.md` requires ("Check authority one time, when work starts... A started request may finish"). Leaving the meeting, plugin retirement and reload still stop the work through the plugin lifecycle. No new authority, custody contract, config or SDK surface.

The original fix is @valkyriweb's (#191059); the `/meet/<code>` URL support that was bundled with it is dropped here so it can land on its own. @jeremynorris diagnosed the same owner in #173896 and #173898.

## User Impact

Google Meet (and the other shared meeting plugins) keep hearing participants and speaking after the join command or agent tool call returns, on both local Chrome and chrome-node. Nothing changes for configured `chrome.audioInputCommand` or while the join is still running.

## Evidence

Real product path on Linux: the Gateway built from each tree (`ocx build --dist`, run as `node dist/entry.js gateway run`), the bundled Google Meet plugin with managed Chromium, `openclaw googlemeet join https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij --mode bidi --transport chrome` from the CLI, and the `google_meet` tool through `tools.invoke`. Chromium maps `meet.google.com` to a local HTTPS fixture page with the Meet lobby and in-call DOM that plays a participant tone; the OpenAI realtime provider points at a local websocket fixture that counts the `input_audio_buffer.append` audio it receives; PipeWire-Pulse is a command fixture. Proof log comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191059#issuecomment-6948130036

Before, `main` 5fb231527f4f (twice via CLI, once via the tool):

```
11:45:05.515 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ googlemeet.join 3468ms
11:45:05.860 [plugins] Meeting browser audio capture failed: Gateway requester authority changed
11:45:05.861 [plugins] Meeting browser audio cleanup failed: Gateway requester authority changed
realtime fixture: appends=2 bytes=43008 at 11:45:09 ... appends=2 bytes=43008 at 11:45:34 (audio stops after the join returns)
```

After, this head 95fcff71fc9e (twice via CLI, once via the tool), no capture or cleanup failure, and an explicit leave still stops capture:

```
11:58:51.512 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ googlemeet.join 3488ms
realtime fixture: appends=8 bytes=143360 at 11:58:53 -> appends=63 bytes=1095680 at 11:59:13
status after 20 s: providerConnected=true bridgeClosed=false realtimeReady=true (main: false / true / false)
11:59:17.994 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ googlemeet.leave 1516ms; appends stop growing after leave
```

Chrome-node transport, real paired node host (Gateway plus a local `openclaw node run` with its own state and managed Chromium, approved with `openclaw devices approve`, same fixtures, `--transport chrome-node`). Full log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191059#issuecomment-6948782370

```
main 5fb231527f4f (x2): capture failed + cleanup failed right after the join; 17-18 node.invoke results between join and leave; model audio stuck at 2 chunks; bridgeClosed=true
this head da7a6104f3f3 (x2, plus once at 95fcff71 with the same production code): no failures; 321-347 node.invoke results between join and leave; model audio ~1.17 MB; bridgeClosed=false providerConnected=true; after leave one node.invoke (bridge stop) and model audio stays flat
```

- Regression tests (red on `main`, green here), one per transport: `realtime-browser-audio-transport.test.ts` and `realtime-node-audio-transport.test.ts` create and start the transport inside a real `withPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope` join scope and owned plugin instance, close that scope's authority after the first pull, and check that the next pull still reaches the browser or node. Production +27/−12, tests +68.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files are clean.
- #167246 (Zoom, agent turn in WebChat) fails through the same transports and the same detached-context fix covers it, but this proof does not exercise an in-turn agent tool call against a model, so it is linked rather than closed.

Credit: @valkyriweb (fix), @jeremynorris (#173896 report and diagnosis, #173898), @GoldenrodScript (#167246), @sukhdeepjohar (#177633, #178413/#178415 precedent, #177973), @xydigitLybnnnn (#167800).

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores the old behavior, and nothing persists. Blast radius: live meeting audio for Google Meet, Zoom, Slack huddles and Teams browser participants.
